recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If patient merge behavior is revisited, handle it under patient/merge-specific issues rather than reopening FHIR-7935's generic search error handling.
issue_request: FHIR-7935 was a Published FHIR-core change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It requested clearer resource integrity/lifecycle guidance for reads and searches involving merged, deleted, redirected, or otherwise modified resource identifiers; the final resolution was to add a section about handling errors with searches.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied in svn revision 5666. The git-svn commit 20dc2f7c4a605bfe418bb4ed6144164271989ea2, headed for the related FHIR-7285 issue, added the source/search.html Handling Errors section that FHIR-7935's Jira comment identifies as revision 5666. A later typo fix, bf1ce05118d8bd16a2bf66b7ac35f69eeb272cd8, corrected the syntactic/logical error sentence.
additional_context: Current source/search.html includes explicit search failure and OperationOutcome guidance, examples for non-existent _id and other logical misses, and _id/logical identifier wording that links search-by-id behavior to Handling Errors. Current source/http.html has the generic Transactional Integrity section, while the detailed search behavior is centralized on the Search page. Later FHIR-9263 clarified Bundle.total handling for OperationOutcome entries, and later FHIR-19687/Patient merge work addresses the broader patient-merge use case separately.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current build source already satisfies the final FHIR-7935 disposition. Duplicating the same rule in the HTTP page would be redundant and could diverge from the active Search page guidance and later patient-specific merge guidance.

related_jiras.note: The same svn revision 5666 commit also resolved the separate missing messaging-search section, explaining why the historical commit headline names #7285 rather than FHIR-7935. It was not decided here because its request is separate.
Clarified that OperationOutcome search outcome entries are not counted in Bundle.total, refining adjacent search outcome behavior without changing the FHIR-7935 conclusion.
Later Patient merge/linking work addresses the broader patient-merge scenario separately from the generic search error-handling guidance.
